ἀετός.as:
ἀετός, -οῦ, ὁ,
[in LXX for נֶשֶׁר;]
an eagle: Re 4:78:13 (Rec. ἀγγέλου) 12:14. Where carrion is referred to, ἀ. is probably a vulture (cf. Jb 39:30, Pr 30:17): Mt 24:28, Lk 17:37 (MM, VGT, s.v.).†

ἀεί.long: always, unceasingly, perpetually; on every occasion.
ἀεί.sd: "ever," by qualification regularly; by implication, earnestly
ἀεί.der: from an obsolete primary noun (apparently meaning continued duration);
ἀεί.as:
ἀεί, adv.,
[in LXX: Is 42:14 (מֵעוֹלָם) 51:13 (תָּמִיד), Ps 94 (95):10, al.;]
ever;
1. of continuous time, unceasingly, perpetually: Ac 7:51, 2 Co 4:11 6:10, Tit 1:12, He 3:10.
2. Of successive occurrences, on every occasion (MM, VGT, s.v.): I Pe 3:15, II Pe 1:12.†
